title.narrative: Activity under preparation Supporting Peacebuilding and Inclusive Dialogue in Myanmar

description.narrative: Myanmar remains affected by protracted armed conflict, deep social fragmentation, and an acute political and economic crisis following the 2021 military coup d¿état. Elections held in January 2026 are projecting an image of normalcy and ¿democratic process¿ but have not been relevant in resolving the crisis, neither by influencing conflict dynamics nor affecting power distribution. The overall objective of the action is to strengthen the resilience and agency of local actors taking a multi-layered peacebuilding approach across individual, community, political and international dimensions. The action is designed to support people, institutions, and processes without conferring political recognition and to maintain EU relevance in a fluid and uncertain transition context. The specific objectives of the action are to: (1) Keep pathways open towards an inclusive and locally led political settlement of the conflict (2) Sustain confidence by strengthening the social contract between communities and local duty bearers(3) Strengthen access to survivor-centred support and accountability pathways for victims of violence and human rights violations.With this additional funding, accountable service delivery functions, partnerships with peace actors and support to victims of human rights violations, from immediate response to strengthening accountability, will be reinforced. The action will integrate a conflict sensitive and rights-based approach. No funding will go directly to political parties, nor to any parties to the conflict. Funding will only be channelled through civil society actors and will not contribute to financial resources of conflict-related and armed actors.The proposed action aims to contribute to the priorities outlined in the amended Regional Multiannual Indicative Programme (MIP) for Asia and the Pacific (2021-2027), in particular the new section ¿1.3.4 ¿ Priority area 4 ¿ Actions in countries in complex settings¿. The action will contribute to the GAP III and its country-level implementation plan (CLIP), in particular its specific objectives 2 and 3[1]. [1] ¿To support access to sexual and reproductive health and prevent and respond to GBV¿ and ¿WROs, other CSOs and women HRDs working for gender equality and women¿s and girls¿ empowerment work more freely and are better protected by law¿
